result.topic_en: Diary entries from May–October 1798 recording results on lemniscatic functions and their series expansions, interpolation of arithmetic-geometric series, arithmetic-geometric and harmonic-geometric means, elliptic transcendents, the rectification of the ellipse, a 'numerico-exponential' calculus, and a probability problem on continued fractions.
result.transcription:
## Numeratorem et denominatorem sinus lemni-
scatii (vniuersalissime accepti) ad quantitates integra-
les reducere contigit; simul omnium functionum
lemniscaticarum quae excogitari possunt, euolutiones
in series infinitas ex principiis genuinis haustae.
inuentum pulcherrimum sane nullique praecedentium inferius
Praeterea iisdem diebus principia deteximus secundum
quae series arithmetico-geometricae interpolari debent, ita
ut [-...-] terminos in progressione data ad [-term-] indicem quem-
cunque rationalem pertinentes per aequationes algebraicas
exhibere iam in potestate sit.          Mai ult. Jun 2.3.
## Inter duos numeros datos {+vt+}[?] [-duo-] semper dantur
infinite multi termini medii tam arithmetico geometrici tum
harmonico geometrici, quorum nexum mutuum ex asse
perspiciendi felicitas nobis est facta.     Junio 3. Brunov.
# Theoriam nostram iam ad transcendentes
ellipticas immediate applicauimus    Junio 5
# Rectificatio Ellipseos tribus modis di- Jun.   10
uersis absoluta.
#Calculum Numerico-Exponentialem omnino no-
uum inuenimus  - - - - -             Jun 12
Problema e calculo probabilitatis circa fractiones continuas olim
frustra tentatum soluimus                    Oct. 25

items.english: I succeeded in reducing the numerator and denominator of the lemniscatic sine (taken in the most general sense) to integral quantities.

items.quote:
Inter duos numeros datos {+vt+}[?] [-duo-] semper dantur
infinite multi termini medii tam arithmetico geometrici tum
harmonico geometrici
items.english: Between two given numbers there are always infinitely many means, both arithmetic-geometric and harmonic-geometric.

items.quote:
Problema e calculo probabilitatis circa fractiones continuas olim
frustra tentatum soluimus
items.english: We solved a problem from the calculus of probability concerning continued fractions, formerly attempted in vain.
